# Introduction

This guide demonstrates the implementation of the approaches proposed in @amendola2025, using the 2019 Poland Household Budget Survey (HBS) to illustrate the estimation of spatial price deflators. The guide is organized into two main sections:

- **[Section 2: Construction of the Consumption Aggregate](cons_agg.qmd)**  
- **[Section 3: Estimation of Price Deflators](price-adj.qmd)**

If your HBS data does not include a consumption aggregate, the diagram below can help determine which section to start with, based on the availability of rent-related data and other key variables. Follow the diagram to assess whether the necessary information is available to conduct the analysis. Even if your HBS data already include a consumption aggregate, you should still examine its sub-components, as explained below.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  Q1["Q1. Does the HBS include<br>food and non-food modules<br>AND inquire rent paid for renters?"]
  Q1 -->|Yes| Q2["Q2. Are self-reported rents<br>available for non-renters?"]
  Q1 -->|No| End1["Stop: This method<br>cannot be used."]

  Q2 -->|Yes| End2["Go to Section 2"]
  Q2 -->|No| Q3["Q3. Does the HBS include a<br>housing module<br>(e.g., roof, floor, etc.)?"]

  Q3 -->|Yes| End2["Go to Section 2"]
  Q3 -->|No| End1["Stop: This method<br>cannot be used."]

  %% Optional: make nodes clickable in HTML output
  %% click Section 1 href "cons_agg.qmd"
```

If your HBS data include a consumption aggregate, examine whether all of its components are available. @deaton2002 and @mancini2022 outline the recommended components of a comprehensive consumption aggregate:

1. Food expenditure items  
2. Non-food nondurable items  
3. Rent paid and imputed rents for non-renters and non-market renters  
4. Durable goods (estimated consumption flow from durable goods)  

In the case of the 2019 HBS data, the fourth component—the consumption flow from durable goods—was not estimated. This is because the BR-04 module (Supplementary Household Information) only collects the number of durable furnishing items owned by households, and only a subset of households was interviewed. Therefore, for the purpose of calculating the price deflator, the consumption aggregate was constructed using components 1–3. 

If you confirm that the available consumption aggregate includes the key components, you may proceed directly to Section 3.

Lastly, before beginning the analysis in the next chapter, we organize the directories, load the required libraries, and source user-defined functions.

```{r, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Set working directory to project root (assumes pl-hbs.Rproj is opened)
path <- "."

# Define folder structure
code <- file.path(path, "code")             # Functions created
data_raw <- file.path(path, "data_raw")     # HBS raw data and auxiliary files (confidential)
data_temp <- file.path(path, "data_temp")   # Intermediate files
data_in <- file.path(path, "data_in")       # Output from Step 1 / Input for Step 2
data_out <- file.path(path, "data_out")     # Final processed outputs
tables <- file.path(path, "tables")         # Table outputs
figures <- file.path(path, "figures")       # Maps and visualizations

# Optional: Clean temp directory (commented out for safety)
# list.files(data_temp, pattern = "*", full.names = TRUE) |> file.remove()

# Load required packages (automatically installs missing ones)
library(pacman)
pacman::p_load(
  dplyr, ggplot2, tidyr, readr, stringr, purrr,
  Hmisc, haven, labelled, skimr, openxlsx, tidyverse,
  broom, janitor, matrixStats, estimatr, modelsummary,
  fastDummies, readxl, survey, knitr, tibble, car,
  robustbase, bestNormalize
)

# Load custom functions
source(file.path(code, "mg_function.R"))     # Merge function
source(file.path(code, "outdetectR.R"))      # Outlier detection
```
